text:
A: Hello! Hi, you can hear me? This is my last one, I think I'm getting better with the buttons now.
B: Hiya! Yeah, loud and clear. I'm Liam. You alright?
A: I'm okay, thank you, bit knackered. I'm Agnieszka, but you can say Aga, is easier.
B: Aga, nice one. Where are you calling from, then?
A: Southampton. I'm from Poland, but I live here almost twenty years now. You?
B: Wakefield, West Yorkshire. And do you know what, I've been to Poland. Krakow, for a mate's stag do. Few years back now.
A: Kraków! Look, I have the magnet on my fridge, behind me. Is beautiful city, no? You saw the old town, the castle?
B: I saw the old town, yeah. Mostly at night, to be fair. I think there was a castle. I've got a photo of it somewhere, I just don't remember taking it.
A: Ha, the stag do, I know, I know. My husband says the English boys in Kraków, every weekend, matching T-shirts.
B: Guilty. Ours were bright orange. What do you do for work, Aga?
A: I'm cleaner, part-time. Offices and GP surgery in city centre. I start six in the morning, the bus is freezing, but is okay. When I saw your picture I think, oh, he looks like the managers in the office I clean. Very tidy, very nice shoes.
B: Ha, I'll take that. Technical sales, heating and air con, so I'm in and out of offices all the time. Out on site visits two or three days a week, I've got the company car, the Audi, so I basically live on the M62.
A: My husband also lives in the car! He is delivery driver, the van. He works too many hours, I tell him, Marek, you are not twenty-five any more. He doesn't listen.
B: They never listen. My girlfriend Jess says the same to me, mind, I'm at the gym at six before work.
A: Six at the gym! For fun? Oh my God. I do only the exercises from the physio, for my hands, and walking on the Common, when my joints are okay. I have arthritis, so some days, erm, is not so good.
B: Oh, sorry to hear that. That must be hard with a physical job and all.
A: Yes, sometimes. I worry I lose hours, you know. But the supervisor is good. I would like a school job maybe, daytime, not so cold in morning. Anyway! You like football? I think from your picture, the mug, the cup.
B: Leeds United mug, yeah, well spotted. Leeds fan for my sins. Do you watch football?
A: No, Marek watches. I like the ski jumping, and volleyball, when Poland plays. I am very loud, my son, Kacper, he goes upstairs, he says Mum, the neighbours.
B: Ski jumping! I've never actually sat and watched it properly. Is it tense?
A: Oh, very! Is like flying, and you think, he will fall, he will fall, and then no, he lands, and I'm screaming in kitchen. Sunday is ski jumping and the rosół, chicken soup, the whole family.
B: That sounds like a good Sunday, to be fair. Mine's meal prep. Chicken, rice, veg, in the boxes for the week.
A: Every day chicken and rice? No, no, this is sad food. You need the pierogi.
B: Jess would agree with you there. She does most of the cooking, I just do a roast and the barbecue. And a curry for tea on a Friday.
A: Tea, you say? For dinner? Here in Southampton they say dinner, but my friend from Liverpool also says tea. I was confused first year, I think she invite me for a cup only!
B: Ha, no, tea's your proper meal up north. You'd have turned up and got fed, don't worry. Oh, is that the timer?
A: Already? Oh, lovely to meet you, Liam. Tell your Jess, more pierogi!
B: I will do. Nice to meet you, Aga, look after yourself!
